title: Yachid, Echad, Kadmon: the sefiros that are not in the Essence and cannot be taken out of it
overview:
The series begins here. Its introduction calls *Shaar HaYichud* a book in two parts: what *hisbonenus* is (not meditation but *iyun*, detailed analytical study, as a doctor must know every particular), and, from chapter 10, what to contemplate: every world and every *sefira* in particulars.

The chapter starts at the top, with the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*, in three levels, *Yachid*, *Echad* and *Kadmon*. The texts say there are no ten *sefiros* there, and they say He engraved letters there, a *Keser* and a *Malchus*. The answer is the kind man. His kindness is not made of kindnesses for shoes and sandwiches; yet a kindness that will not do shoes is no kindness at all, "just a bureaucracy", and the pants he never gave are in it too. So with the *Aibershter*: take out one *sefira* and you are a *kofer*; and in the *nimshal* the actual sandwich, the actual car, comes from there. In the soul the same three levels run from powers that *mamash* do not exist, through powers ready to come out, to the estimate of one grab for the vodka bottle; and to reach the physical it takes a *tzimtzum*.

sections.title: From here on: every world, every sefira, in particulars
sections.summary: The first part of the book taught that *hisbonenus* is detailed study; from chapter 10 the book begins the subject itself, the four worlds and their *sefiros* down to particulars of particulars, and how each world's *Keser* joins it to the one above.

blocks.text:
*Shaar HaYichud*, the Gate of Unification, of the *Mitteler Rebbe*, Rabbi DovBer, the second Lubavitcher Rebbe, is called the Key to Kabbala and *Chassidus*, and also *Kuntres HaHisbonenus*, the book of contemplation. Its first part explains what *hisbonenus* (contemplation) is; the second, from chapter 10, what to contemplate.

The first part continues his *Kuntres HaHispaalus*, on awakening the G-dly emotions, love and fear of G-d, which says there is no real *hispaalus* (awakening of the emotions) without proper *hisbonenus* before it.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the introduction to the series (tape 001), which reads no line: it presents the book and says why the classes begin at chapter 10, so it is placed under the chapter's opening.

blocks.text: *Hisbonenus* is not, as most people think, meditation, which is based on concentration. It is a synonym for what the Talmud calls *iyun*: deep, repetitive, analytical study, the kind any subject needs. You go over the subject again and again, each time in a slightly new way, and each time you discover new angles in it.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the introduction to the series (tape 001), which reads no line: it presents the book and says why the classes begin at chapter 10, so it is placed under the chapter's opening.

blocks.title: The doctor and the engineer
blocks.text: To become an adept at any subject one has to study it in detail. Most of us know in general what medicine is about, or engineering, or chemistry, and that does not make us a doctor or an engineer or a chemist. A doctor has to know the particulars: all the parts of the human body, all the different medicines and all the different maladies, and which medicine works for which malady. The same with any other subject. And the deeper the subject, the more one has to study it, and the more detail, and the more kinds of explanation, one needs to become an adept at it.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the introduction to the series (tape 001), which reads no line: it presents the book and says why the classes begin at chapter 10, so it is placed under the chapter's opening.

blocks.text: Since the subject of Kabbala and *Chassidus* is G-dliness, it is the deepest study there is and needs the most study. It is not possible "to just go to a cave someplace and meditate on G-dliness and expect to become an adept." The subject is totally unknowable by the human mind and cannot be arrived at by human effort. The only way is the Kabbala G-d gave on Mount Sinai: with the written and oral Torah He gave Moses all its explanations, the kabbalistic explanations of G-dliness among them.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the introduction to the series (tape 001), which reads no line: it presents the book and says why the classes begin at chapter 10, so it is placed under the chapter's opening.

blocks.text: *Hisbonenus*, deep analytical study, has to be joined by concentration, during the study and after: without concentrating one gets no benefit from studying, and after studying one has to think about it. What one learns is the *seder hishtalshelus* (the chaining down of the worlds): how all four universes, emanation, creation, formation and action, come down from the infinite light, something from nothing, to our physical universe. One has to know all the details, and then contemplate what one learned.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the introduction to the series (tape 001), which reads no line: it presents the book and says why the classes begin at chapter 10, so it is placed under the chapter's opening.

blocks.text: That is a synopsis of the first part of the book: *hisbonenus* is not meditative concentration, focusing the mind on a single thing, but a deep analytical study of all the details of the chain of worlds from the infinite light down to ours. So the course begins at chapter 10, where the second part begins and the book starts to explain what the *hisbonenus* will be on.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the introduction to the series (tape 001), which reads no line: it presents the book and says why the classes begin at chapter 10, so it is placed under the chapter's opening.

blocks.text: The general framework: how the four worlds come down from the infinite light. Before the worlds, the whole space where they are now was full of the absolutely infinite light of G-dliness. To make room for a world, G-d, so to speak, removed the light from a place, "like a ball," a sphere. Into it He emanated a very thin line of light, finite compared with the infinite light, and through more and more *tzimtzumim* (lessenings of the light) brought it down to the very finite world we live in.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the introduction to the series (tape 001), which reads no line: it presents the book and says why the classes begin at chapter 10, so it is placed under the chapter's opening.

blocks.text: To recap: the removal of the light is the first *tzimtzum*. What was left is a *reshimu*, an impression of the light, and from it He drew the thin, finite line from which the worlds were created. Each world has less light, from emanation down through creation, formation and action, and at the end of action is the world of the *kelipos*, the shells or externalities, "sometimes called evil influences," where we are. So in this world evil is possible, and it can seem as if there is no G-d.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the introduction to the series (tape 001), which reads no line: it presents the book and says why the classes begin at chapter 10, so it is placed under the chapter's opening.

blocks.text: "Now, chapter 10." Having told us that *hisbonenus* has to be done *derech prat* (in detail), he now explains in detail all the particulars of the ten *sefiros* of the four worlds: "this is what he's going to explain, everything."

Every *sefira* divides into particulars of particulars: *chesed* of *Malchus* of *chachma* of *Malchus* of *chesed*, "any five levels." When you finish this you should be able to figure it out; and *v'chahai gavna*, "and the like," means even six levels.

phrases.he: וענין יחודם והתכללותם בבחינת הכתר שבכל עולם,
phrases.en: How everything is included in the *Keser* of each world,

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת הממוצע בין עולם העליון לתחתון הימנו
כידוע הכלל דרך קיצור
שמבחינת מלכות שבעליון נעשה כתר לתחתון, עד רום המעלות.

blocks.text: How all is included in the *Keser* of each world, the intermediary to the world below, since the *Malchus* of the upper becomes the *Keser* of the lower: "that's what is going to be explained in chapter 10 through the end of the book."

sections.title: First the Source of everything: the Essence before the tzimtzum, in three levels
sections.summary: Before the worlds, one has to contemplate *Mekora d'Kula*, the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*, and that too in particulars. In general it divides into three levels, *Yachid*, *Echad* and *Kadmon*, each of ten *sefiros*, all still inside the *Atzmus*.

phrases.he: אך הנה מתחלה
phrases.en: However, now that we're getting started, first of all

phrases.he: יש לכל מתבונן להתבונן במקור הראשון
הנקרא מקורא דקולא
phrases.en: the source of everything,

phrases.he: שהוא בבחינת עצמות אור אין סוף
שלפני הצמצום הנקרא מקום פנוי הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: before the *tzimtzum*, which is called the *makom panui*.

blocks.text: First of all, the contemplator has to start with the first source, *Mekora d'Kula*, the source of everything: the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* (the infinite light) before the *tzimtzum*, the *tzimtzum* called the *makom panui* (the empty space).

phrases.he: גם שם דרך פרט דוקא
phrases.en: And over there we're also going to look in a way of a *derech prat*.

phrases.he: והוא הנקרא מאריך באחד, באחדות הפשוטה דוקא
phrases.en: This is the inner meaning of *ma'arich b'echad* in *Hashem Elokeinu Hashem Echad*: he looks at length *b'achdus hapeshuta davka*.

blocks.text: There too we look *derech prat*. That is the inner meaning of *ma'arich b'echad*, drawing out the *Echad* of "*Hashem Elokeinu Hashem Echad*": one looks at length into the simple oneness.

phrases.he: ונחלק לג' מדריגות דרך כלל
phrases.en: In general we divide it into three levels.

phrases.he: ובכל א' כלול מי׳ ספירות
phrases.en: Each one of them includes within it ten *sefiros*.

phrases.he: והוא יחיד ואחד וקדמון,
phrases.en: These three levels: *Yachid*, *Echad* and *Kadmon*.

phrases.he: והכל בבחינת עצמות אור אין סוף שלפני הצמצום הראשון הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: This all is still inside the *Atzmus*.

blocks.text: **In general** it divides into three levels; really into many more, since these three are only the *pnimiyus ha'or* (the inner aspect of the light), which then has its *hispashtus ha'or* (spreading forth). He is not even talking about the *Maor* (the source of the light) here, but about the *etzem ha'or*, the light itself, the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof*. Each level includes ten *sefiros*: *Yachid* (singular), *Echad* (one) and *Kadmon* (preceding), "all still inside the *Atzmus*."

sections.title: Yachid: no ten sefiros, and yet ten sefiros included
sections.summary: *Yachid* is *mamash* alone, above even a unification, so in the Essence one cannot speak of ten *sefiros*. Yet just as speech shows a will and a brain behind it, the Essence includes ten *sefiros*: wise, but not with a wisdom you could separate out. The *middos* come from Him; they do not describe Him.

phrases.he: בחינת יחיד משמעו לבדו ממש
והוא למעלה מהתאחדות נפרדים
שנקרא אחד כידוע
ולפי זה בבחינת העצמות ממש
לא יתכן לומר עדיין ענין עשר ספירות כלל
וכמו מלכות דאין סוף,
שממילא מובן שקדם לזה בחינת כתר וחכמה כו'

blocks.title: Speech means a will and a brain
blocks.text: So in the Essence itself one cannot yet speak of ten *sefiros* at all. The comparison is *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*, which by itself shows that *Keser* and *chachma* came before it. *Malchus* means speech: "You can't have a speech without a *ratzon* (will) and a brain."

phrases.he: ובאמת גם בבחינת העצמות דאור אין סוף
שנקרא לבדו
כלול בעצמו י׳ ספירות
אך שנקרא חכים לא בחכמה ידיעא כידוע,
phrases.en: He is wise, but not with a wisdom that can be separated out so you can know that this is the wisdom.

phrases.he: עד ולאו מכל אלין מדות כלל.
phrases.en: It's not just that *lav b'chachma yedia*; it really is not of these *middos* at all.

blocks.text: Even the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof*, called *Levado*, includes ten *sefiros*. By the way, in *Emek HaMelech* (a Kabbalistic work) he calls the *Maor* and the *Levad* levels of *Yachid*. So here he is talking about the most external level of *Yachid*, which is the most inward level of the *Or Ein Sof*.

"Wise, but not with a known wisdom": not with a discernible *chachma*. Mainly, He is wise, but not with a wisdom that can be separated out so you can know "this is the wisdom." "And not of any of these attributes at all": He really is not of these *middos* at all. "Just the opposite, the *middos* come from him," not that they describe Him in any way.

sections.title: His light as He is, and yet letters engraved: a Keser and a Malchus in the Essence
sections.summary: The *Or Ein Sof* is simple like the Essence, "He and His Name", the *tehiru ila'a*, a revelation of Him to Himself, where even "unity" does not fit. The names wise and kind are only from what He would be after the *tzimtzum*; and yet the Zohar's *glif glifu* puts a head and an end, a *Keser* and a *Malchus*, inside the Essence: "*Ana Emloch*", which the souls of Israel precede.

phrases.he: והענין הוא
דבאמת כמו שעצמות האין סוף הוא אור פשוט בתכלית הפשיטות,
כך ממש בחינת אורו וזיוו הנקרא אור אין סוף
דהיינו הוא ושמו בלבד כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: That means only Him and His name.

blocks.text: He is talking first about the *Maor*: the Essence is a light utterly simple, and so *mamash* (actually) is His light and radiance, the *Or Ein Sof*: "only Him and His Name." The *bilvad* (only) is "like a total hint," not explained here. Simply, there is no other level; but really it is within the matter of *Levado*. "Him" is the *Atzmus Ein Sof*; "His Name" is the *Or Ein Sof*.

phrases.he: והוא הנקרא טהירו עילאה
שזהו ענין ובחינת התגלות אור עצמותו כמו שהוא דוקא
phrases.en: That is the revelation of the light of Himself, exactly how He is.

blocks.text: This whole matter of the *tehiru ila'a* is everything before the *tzimtzum*. *Kadmon* too is still *tehiru ila'a*, not only *Yachid*.

**That is the revelation of the light of Himself, exactly how He is**: the actual revelation. Elsewhere it is explained that the *etzem Atzmus Or Ein Sof* is a revelation to Himself, not yet the revelation that goes out to others: "It's *mamash* to nobody."

phrases.he: והוא הנקרא יחיד,
phrases.en: This is what is called *Yachid*:

phrases.he: שאין עוד מלבדו
phrases.en: there's no more besides Him,

phrases.he: לומר בו לשון התאחדות או לשון יחוד
phrases.en: that you really cannot even call it a unification or a unity.

phrases.he: וזהו אנת הוא חד ולא בחושבן י' כו'.
phrases.en: You are one and not with a *cheshbon*, not with a mathematics. Which mathematics? Ten: that's ten *sefiros*.

blocks.text: **This is what is called *Yachid***, *ein od milvado*: **there's no more besides Him**. But this is its most external part, its actual *gilui* (revelation), "almost *hispashtus* of it." So **you really cannot even call it a unification or a unity**; it does not apply. "Even to call it *Yachid* is wrong," since *Yachid* is a word of *yichud*, unity.
It says *Ant hu chad v'lo b'chushban*: You are one, and not with a count, "not with a mathematics." Which mathematics? The commentary on it says "ten": that is the ten *sefiros*.

phrases.he: אך מה שאמרו חכים ולא בחכמה ידיעא כו'
phrases.en: So why do they say He is wise, but not with a known wisdom?

phrases.he: שיש על כל פנים חלוקי מדריגות,
חכים ומבין חסדן ורחמן כו'
הכל לא מצד עצמותו,
phrases.en: This thing that we're calling *chacham* is not really that it actually describes Him.

phrases.he: רק מצד מה ששיער בעצמו בכח
מה שעתיד להיות בפועל אחר הצמצום הראשון הנזכר לעיל

blocks.question: Then why say He is wise, but not with a known wisdom, as if He had levels? If there is no *chachma* there, how is He wise?
blocks.text: What we call *chacham* (wise) "is not really that it actually describes him": since He made people with *chachma* and *bina*, you have to say He is a *chacham*. But what do you mean, you have to? "We just said there is no *chachma*."

Usually "this guy has no *chachma*" means he is stupid. Said of the *Aibershter* (the One Above), it means not a lack of *chachma* but **not with a known wisdom**: not like your *chachma*, so far beyond it that you cannot say *chachma* there.

More: the whole matter of *chachma* comes from Him. *Chachma* does not define Him; He defines the *chachma*, and it gets everything from Him. By a *chacham*, what defines him is that he is a *chacham*.

Another thing: as we learned before, *chachma* also means stupidity. *Taanug* (delight) too is the power to have pleasure or the opposite: the ability to feel pain comes from *pnimiyus haKeser* of *Atik*, like the ability to feel pleasure. So the ability to be stupid also comes from Him, and if He is wise, not with a known wisdom, "you'll have to say also he's stupid," not with a known stupidity: a *shtus d'kedusha* (holy foolishness).

sensitivity.reason: Says that G-d is "stupid, not with a known stupidity"; some readers would take the wording as irreverent, like the film joke after it.
sensitivity.publishable: Another thing: as we learned before, *chachma* also includes its opposite. *Taanug* (delight) too is the power to have pleasure or the opposite: the ability to feel pain comes from *pnimiyus haKeser* of *Atik*, like the ability to feel pleasure. So the ability to lack wisdom also comes from Him, and if He is wise, not with a known wisdom, the opposite of wisdom is in Him too, not as you think it: a *shtus d'kedusha* (holy foolishness).

blocks.text: Nobody can beat the *Aibershter*: "If you're going to play a stupid game, the *Aibershter* would win. You know, like they had a movie, *Dumb and Dumber*. If there was a contest who could be the dumbest of them all, the *Aibershter* would win."

sensitivity.reason: A joke that G-d would win a contest for the dumbest, by way of a film comedy; some readers would take it as irreverent.

blocks.text: This is part of what we mean by "the place": "There has to be a place for stupidity. Think about it. Otherwise you couldn't have a stupid person." So too He gives existence to the *chachma*, so that *chachma* means both lines.

phrases.he: (וכמו שכתוב במקדש מלך בלשון האריז''ל עצמו ומבואר במקום אחר באריכות)
phrases.en: This is explained in the *Mikdash Melech*.

phrases.he: וזהו ענין כללות המאמר הראשון בזוהר,
בריש הורמנא דמלכא גליף גליפו בטהירו עילאה
פירוש בעצמות גלוי אורו הפשוט הנזכר לעיל שנקרא טהירו עילאה,
גליף גליפו שהוא ענין חקיקת אותיות
phrases.en: He engraved letters,

blocks.text:
This is explained in *Mikdash Melech* (a commentary on the Zohar); "this little blurb here is a reference," a footnote.

Then the first saying of the *Zohar*: "He engraved an engraving," the engraving of letters. Later we will learn that within the *ratzon hapashut* (the simple will) is the *ratzon hamuchlat* (the absolute will): that is the engraving of letters.

phrases.he: ובריש הורמנא,
שזה כשעלה ברצונו הפשוט,
הוא בחינת כתר,
ובחינת האותיות שחקק
הוא בחינת המלכות דאור אין סוף
ואם כן יש ראש וסוף,
כתר ומלכות, גם בבחינת עצמיות אור אין סוף

blocks.text: When it arose in His simple will, the *Keser*, that He wants a certain thing, and in the letters He engraved, the *Malchus*: so the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* has a head and an end. And a *chachma*: how else did He figure out how to make letters? "A dog can have a *ratzon* and he can't write it." And *bina*, to divide into letters; and presumably, with *bina*, *middos*.

phrases.he: וביאורו
שעלה במחשבה ורצון הפשוט
phrases.en: When it came up in the *ratzon hapashut*

phrases.he: אנא אמלוך
phrases.en: "I will rule."

phrases.he: והכל בעצמותו עדיין,
phrases.en: This is still inside of Himself.

phrases.he: קודם ענין מה ששיער בעצמו בכח דוקא כל מה שיהיה לו רצון למלוכה בגלוי,
phrases.en: This is still before He actually figured out.

phrases.he: והוא אחר הצמצום הנקרא מקום פנוי כו'
phrases.en: The *shiur* is what will be after the *tzimtzum*.

blocks.question: You told us there is no *Keser* and *Malchus* there; now you say there is?
blocks.text: He has done this several times already: there is and there isn't. The explanation: it arose in the thought and the simple will, "*Ana Emloch*" (I shall rule).

blocks.title: With whom did He consult? The Jews before "I shall rule"
blocks.text: "Over here there's a little thing I always stick in": *b'mi nimlach?* With whom did He consult? *B'nishmoseihem shel tzaddikim*, with the souls of the *tzaddikim*. *Emloch* is "I will rule," *nimlach* "consult," "basically the same word": when He said *Ana Emloch*, through whom did He become king? And "Your people are all *tzaddikim*." So the source of a Jew is in the *Ana Emloch*, higher than the *machshava kduma* (the primordial thought), and really higher than the *Ana Emloch* itself: they gave it existence. "The Jews go all the way up."

All this is still within His Essence, before He figured it out. It is the *glif glifu* (He engraved an engraving), which has levels: in *Yachid*, in *Echad*, and in *Kadmon*, where the *shiur* (estimation) is. Usually the *glif glifu* is said to be a *shiur*, but here he puts it before the *shiur*, in the simple will, and not even in *Echad*: in *Yachid*. So in *Yachid* itself there is a *glif glifu*: "the actual decision for the Jew is in *Yachid*."

More: the *Or Ein Sof* of *Yachid* is the revelation of the *Atzmus* exactly as it is, so a *glif glifu* in it came from the *Atzmus*. "Really it's the *Aibershter* that wants the Jew"; otherwise the Jew could not exist, since He is the place of everything, and the light cannot do what He gives no place for. It goes even higher, though the text speaks only of the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof*.
Which is after the *tzimtzum*: the *shiur* is what will be after the *tzimtzum*. So what is going on? From one side it is a perfect unity with no parts, and then we talk about parts.

sections.title: The kind man: a hiyuli desire for kindness that holds every particular
sections.summary: A kind person's kindness is not made of kindnesses for shoes and sandwiches, yet a kindness that lacks one of them is no kindness at all, and every particular, even pants he never gave, comes out of it. So too the ten *sefiros* are in the Essence: not as parts, and not removable, and in the *nimshal* the actual sandwich comes from there.

phrases.he: והדמיון בזה ידוע
מכחות הנפש בהתגלות מרצון עד המעשה
שישנם כולם בפרט
בהעלם אור עצמות הנפש שנקרא בחינת יחידה

blocks.text: They are all there, in particular: the powers. The *yechida* (the essence of the soul) is a unitary thing, not made up of powers, "but nonetheless you have to say that the powers are there."

phrases.he: כמו על דרך דוגמא
כאשר האדם הוא חפץ חסד וטוב להטיב בדבר פרט,
שזהו בא מצד שיש בו מדה זאת דחפץ חסד וטוב בבחינת עצמות נפשו, הנקרא יחידה
phrases.en: It means that he is a kind person himself.

phrases.he: על כן בא חפץ חסד זה בגלוי מן העלמו
phrases.en: That's why this *chafetz chesed* comes into revelation from its hiddenness.

blocks.text: It means he himself is a kind person. "Wait a minute, how can you say that the himself is kind? The himself is just the himself. It's not made up of *middos*." True; but if he is kind, he is not just him plus "different kind of add-ons." He himself is kind, so there has to be a kindness there: not a separate thing, but still a particular.

blocks.title: The schnorrers' recommendation
blocks.text:
That is why the desire for kindness comes out into the open. You see it by the *schnorrers* (beggars), who tell each other where to go. "Go to this one, he's a good guy, he'll help you." "How do you know? What, do you know the future?" "I don't have to know the future. He's a good guy." "Did you see his goodness?" "No, but he helped me, and he helped Shloimy, and he helped Chaimy. So he must be a good guy."

Not that he *has* a kindness: then "maybe he got hit on the head and the kindness kind of went away." "No, he's a good guy himself." That is why the *chafetz chesed* comes out of its hiddenness, and he helped me, and Shloimy, and Chaimy.

phrases.he: ומוכרח לומר בוודאי
phrases.en: So you have to say for sure

phrases.he: שחפץ חסד זה בעצמות נפשו הוא בבחינת כח היולי בעצמיות
phrases.en: that the *chafetz chesed* is a *hiyuli*,

phrases.he: לכלול כל מה שעתיד לחפוץ בחסד וטוב
phrases.en: any kind of good thing.

phrases.he: בכל פרטי פרטי הענינים שיבקשו ממנו
phrases.en: It includes all the different particular things that people will ask from him.

blocks.title: Shoes, coats, sandwiches, and pants
blocks.text: It is not a kindness like this. "What did he do for you?" "I needed shoes, he gave me shoes." "And for Chaimy?" "A coat." "And Shloimy?" "He was hungry, a sandwich." "So he has a kindness for shoes, a kindness for coats and a kindness for sandwiches. But I need pants. Do you know anybody he gave pants to?" "No, but he has a kindness. Tell him you need pants, he'll give you pants." How do you know? He never gave pants to anybody. Because the *chafetz chesed* is a *hiyuli*.

To include everything he will ever want of kindness and good, any good thing, in all the particulars of particulars that will be asked of him: "If you'll go and ask him for pants, it's included in the *hiyuli*."

Next side, after the foundation example (4:22), he sums up: the essential, *hiyuli* desire for kindness includes all the particular things people will ask of him, "like we said, shoes, sandwiches, whatever," and he reads the two lines again from "the third line here."

More: if one particular is missing, it is not *chesed*. It is not made up of the particulars: a person's essential *chafetz chesed* is not made of *ratzonos* (wills) to give sandwiches, shoes and clothing; what defines it is *chesed*, kindness. "However, if you take out one *prat*, it means it's not *chesed* anymore."

So it says in *Pasach Eliyahu* (Elijah's opening prayer, in the *Tikkunei Zohar*): whoever separates one of these ten *sefiros* from its fellow, it is as if he separated You. The *Atzmus* is not made of the *sefiros*, but say "I'm going to take out *chesed*," and "it's not the *Aibershter* anymore. He's a *kofer* (denier) in the whole *Aibershter*."

For instance, if one says "G-d is love," with no *din* (judgement), or, as some people say, "G-d is unconditional love," one has taken out the attribute of *din*, and the attribute of *din* says there are conditions.

Same as "this guy will do anything for you, but he won't give you shoes; walking around without shoes, too bad": that is not kindness anymore. So though He is not made of the ten *sefiros*, take out one and it is no longer the *Aibershter*: "as if he separated You."

phrases.he: ואם כן בהכרח
phrases.en: So you have to say

phrases.he: שקודם שעלה ברצונו וחפצו זה שבגלוי,
להטיב חסדו בדבר זה הפרטי,
היה כלול בעצמיות חפץ חסד ההיולי
phrases.en: that the *chesed* for shoes was included in the *chafetz chesed hahiyuli*.

phrases.he: ויצא מן ההיולי להתגלות בדבר פרטי זה
phrases.en: And it came out from the *hiyuli* to be *misgaleh* in this particular kindness.

blocks.text: **So you have to say** that a *chesed* for pants was included: a *chesed* for pants came out, and how could it, if it was not there? Yet the essential *chafetz chesed* is not made up of *chassadim* (kindnesses) for pants and coats and sandwiches. So from one side you have to say that the pants and coats and sandwiches are there.

In the *nimshal* (what the analogy stands for) you *mamash* have to say it. In the *mashal*, a kind person's *hiyuli* desire includes a *chesed* for sandwiches, but no actual sandwich: the sandwiches are external, and "unless he's a rich guy" he cannot keep giving them out. In the *nimshal*, the actual sandwich comes from there.

"And this is the thing that people tend to fail to understand." They see it as more and more abstract. In the *mashal*, never mind a sandwich, even to say there is a *chesed* for sandwiches in the *chafetz chesed* "is stupid": it is not a *chesed* for sandwiches, it is a *chesed*. "But by the *Aibershter* it's the same thing."

blocks.title: Thanking Him for an idea of a sandwich
blocks.text: You can't say the *Aibershter* has sandwiches up there. "I ate a sandwich, and you told me to *bentsh* because the *Aibershter* gave me the sandwich. If He didn't have this physical sandwich, why thank Him? Let me thank whoever gave me the physical sandwich." Yet you bless before and after: the actual sandwich came from there, so the *Aibershter* has sandwiches. "In a way it's a stupid thing to say, but in a way it's a stupid thing to say the opposite also": without them, where do they come from?

So the essential *chafetz chesed* is a *hiyuli* power that includes whatever particular things they will ask of him. (He reads the line again.) The *chafetz chesed* for sandwiches had to be included in it, to the point that without it the *hiyuli* desire for kindness "is totally not a *chafetz chesed*." Take the particular out, and there is no *chesed*. What does that mean?

blocks.title: The foundation that only gives shoes
blocks.text: There are foundations whose charter is to give shoes. A man can "drop dead on the floor from starvation" there, and they will not give him a sandwich: their charter is shoes. It might have started from a kind man who would have given a sandwich too; now it is a foundation, and it gives shoes. Is this a *chesed*? No, it is not a *chesed* anymore.

sensitivity.reason: Charitable foundations are pictured as letting a man starve on their floor because of their charter.
sensitivity.publishable: Picture a foundation whose charter is to give shoes. A starving man asks for a sandwich, and they will not give him one: their charter is shoes. It might have started from a kind man who would have given a sandwich too; now it is a foundation, and it gives shoes. Is this a *chesed*? No, it is not a *chesed* anymore.

blocks.text: A kindness that has become bound by a charter still takes care of shoes, but it does not give because of goodness any more, even though it originated with goodness: "now it is just bureaucracy."
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 003 opens by finishing the foundation example of tape 002 on these lines, before it reads line lwzq6db4 again at 4:43.

sensitivity.reason: Calls charitable foundations a bureaucracy that no longer acts from goodness.
sensitivity.publishable: A kindness that has become bound by a charter still takes care of shoes, but it does not give because of goodness any more, even though it originated with goodness.

blocks.title: Communism, a kindness of Tohu
blocks.text: "Some of the worst, terriblest things in the world came out of goodness, actually, like communism." Marx and Engels were maybe "slightly misguided," but the original idea was that everybody's needs should be met, and then it got separated from the *Atzmus*: *olam haTohu*, a *chesed* of *Tohu*. It will give shoes to somebody, and somebody else can *mamash* starve to death and it will not help him.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 003 opens by finishing the foundation example of tape 002 on these lines.

blocks.text: A real *chesed* is not like the foundation, where you cannot say, "These are kind people, go to them." "I don't need shoes, I got shoes. I need a coat." "Sorry, we don't give coats." "It's not a *chesed* anymore, it's just a bureaucracy." So without the particular the whole *chesed* is not there: if he has all kinds of kindnesses but won't give you a sandwich, he is not a kind guy, and whatever he does it for, it is not kindness. So this particular was included in the essence of the *hiyuli* desire for kindness, and came out of it.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 003 opens by finishing the foundation example of tape 002 on these lines.

blocks.text: So too by the *Aibershter*. From one side He is above anything; from the other, you have to say that the *Aibershter* has sandwiches. "If he's missing one sandwich, he's not the *Aibershter*."
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 003 opens by finishing the foundation example of tape 002 on these lines.

blocks.text: "And not only kosher sandwiches. He's got *treif* (non-kosher) sandwiches."
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 003 opens by finishing the foundation example of tape 002 on these lines.

sensitivity.reason: Says G-d "has treif sandwiches"; a joke of the same kind as the Dumb and Dumber one, which some readers would take as irreverent.

blocks.title: "He ain't got no money"
blocks.text: "Mine is the silver and Mine is the gold" is translated to mean *chesed* and *gevura*, but really it means it literally. In *Shemoneh Esrei* (the eighteen blessings) we ask, "Give me money." "What are you going to Him for money for? He ain't got no money." "Doesn't mean that He ain't got no money. It means that what He's got is way past money. Doesn't mean that He's poor. If He wants, He can give you money. *Mamash* money."
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 003 opens by finishing the foundation example of tape 002 on these lines.

phrases.he: ואנו רואים שיש בחפץ חסד זה שכל וחכמה ומדות ומחשבה ודבור ומעשה
phrases.en: We see that when the *chafetz chesed* of the *atzmiyus* comes into actuality, we see that there's a *sechel*.

phrases.he: אם כן ודאי במקור חפץ חסד זה בהעלמו,
כשהיה כלול בעצמיות החפץ חסד ההיולי,
גם כן מהתחלקות שכל ומדות ומחשבה דבור ומעשה שבו
phrases.en: There also had to be a division of these things.

blocks.title: The drunk who says his family is starving
blocks.text: When the essential *chafetz chesed* comes into actuality there is a *sechel* (intellect) in it: you have to figure out exactly how to do the *chesed*. "This guy is telling me his family is starving, but I know this guy's a drunk. If I give him money he'll spend it on liquor and come home and beat up his family. So I'm going to send a bunch of food over to his wife, not to him." That shows there has to be a *sechel*.

To do the *chesed* there are *middos*: he has to feel a *chesed* and a pity in his heart. Then *machshava* (thought), "Okay, so let's do this"; *dibur* (speech), when the guy asks, "Okay, I'll help you"; and *maaseh* (action). So there are ten *sefiros*: *sechel* is *chachma*, then all the *middos*, and thought, speech and action are *Malchus*.
there was also the division: otherwise, how could it come out like that? The revealed *chesed* has ten *sefiros*, so the hidden *chesed* also had to have ten *sefiros*.

phrases.he: אבל בבחינת עצמיות חפץ חסד ההיולי,
כמו שהוא קודם שבא עדיין בדבר פרטי,
הגם שבודאי גם שם יש התחלקות שכל ומדות כו',
מכל מקום כלולים ומתאחדים בתכלית

blocks.text: As with the shoes and the sandwiches: they were not two *chassadim* unified in the sense of connected together to build a bigger *chesed*; "there really wasn't two separate things, it was only one thing." So too the ten *sefiros* of the essential *chafetz chesed*.

Later he says the same of the essential *chafetz chesed* in the *Atzmus Ein Sof*: the kindness in a person's *yechida* is no more separate than the shoes from the sandwiches, or than its own ten *sefiros*; nor is it separate from the other *sefiros*, or really from the *Atzmus*.

sections.title: Every attribute alike, down to kingship: "I shall rule"
sections.summary: *Chesed* is only the example; every attribute, *netzach* with its strategy and its pep talk, down to *Malchus*, is made of ten, all one before it comes to a particular. He picked *chesed* and *Malchus* because the world comes from the desire for kindness and from "*Ana Emloch*": there is no king without a people.

phrases.he: וכמו כן במדה פרטית אחרת שבעצמיות,
כמו מדת הגבורה והתפארת והנצח וכהאי גוונא
עד בחינת המלכות
phrases.en: all the way to *Malchus*,

phrases.he: שהוא מדת ההתנשאות
שכלול בודאי מי',
phrases.en: Certainly, same like all the other *sefiros*, it's made up from ten *sefiros*,

phrases.he: רצון וחפץ למלוכה וחכמה ומדות ומחשבה כו'.

blocks.text: *Chafetz chesed* is just the example; every other attribute in the essence is like that, *gevura*, *tiferes*, *netzach* and the like. A guy who likes to win, for instance, has the attribute of *netzach* (victory) in his soul.

blocks.title: The football game
blocks.text: He likes to win all kinds of things, in all their particulars, and to win he needs a *sechel* and *middos*: "even though it's a stupid football game," there is a strategy to it.

blocks.title: It's all strategy
blocks.text: "Everybody here is into football." They talk, he has no idea what they are talking about, and after a while they look at him for his comment. He says, "Yeah, you know, it's all strategy." And they say, "Yeah, right, that's right."

What does "strategy" mean? That in *netzach* there has to be a *sechel*. Then *middos*: in the pep talk before the game "he's trying to build up their *middos*." And there are thought, speech and action in the *netzach*.

Any attribute could carry a *mashal*; he gave it on *chesed*, "and by the way, I think he picked *chesed* in particular because the world comes from *chafetz chesed*." Then down to *Malchus*, the attribute of *hisnasus* the world came out from. It too is made of ten: the will to rule (*Keser*), *chachma*, *middos*, and thought, speech and action, *Malchus* of *Malchus*.

phrases.he: אך קודם שבא לבחינת התגלות בדבר פרט,
phrases.en: But before it became *hisgalus* for a particular thing,

phrases.he: כמו למלוך על מדינה זו וכהאי גוונא,
כלולים ומתאחדים בתכלית
בבחינת מדת המלוכה ההיולית העצמית
כמו בעצמות חפץ חסד ההיולי הנ"ל

blocks.text: Now he goes back to the *Ana Emloch*, the *glif glifu*: that is why he came back *davka* to *Malchus*. The *chafetz chesed* was the arousal from above that brought about a world in the first place, but the actual thing of the world was *Ana Emloch*, *Malchus*, the *glif glifu*, which is letters, *Malchus*. It is also *hisnasus* over another, which brings about the existence of another: "there is no king without a people."

But before it was revealed in a particular thing, like ruling over this country, there was the original attribute of kingship: its *hiyuli* existed before it happened. They are wholly included in the essential, *hiyuli* attribute of kingship, as we said before.

sections.title: Not even "unified": the powers within the soul's essence, and where the particulars come from
sections.summary: Tape 004 picks up in mid-discussion (lines 48 to 64 are not recorded): the eye has the power to see every shape, even a sofa some guy in China has, and the will for *chesed* holds a will for every particular, or where would they come from? In the *nimshal* not only the power comes from there: the actual sofa, the actual car, the physical world itself.

phrases.he: מזה מוכרח לומר
שיש כל פרטים הללו בהתפשטות הכלולה בעצם לגמרי,
שאם לא כן מאין נמצאו פרטים הללו בגלוי ההתפשטות
phrases.en: Where did it come from?

blocks.question: The eye has a *hiyuli* for round and square shapes. What about a sofa some guy in China has, which you never saw and never will?
blocks.text: The eye has the power to see that too, and not only if it were exposed to it: the power to see that shape already exists in the eye, and so in the soul. All the shapes exist in the soul. ("But that's really the power to see the shapes, not the actual sofa itself." "Right.")
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 004 opens in the middle of a discussion, before it reads line 5jn5xeq5; the reading of the lines before it is not recorded, and the discussion leads straight into this line.

blocks.text: So with the will for *chesed*: a will to give a sandwich, or a shoe, is not the actual shoe. That is in the *mashal*. In the *nimshal* the actual shoe comes out from it, and the actual sofa, and all a person's emotions: the whole of *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, down to the final physicality. "Mine is the silver and Mine is the gold" does not mean just the ability to earn money; the actual thing comes out of there.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 004 opens in the middle of a discussion, before it reads line 5jn5xeq5; it leads into this line.

blocks.title: Where did my car come from?
blocks.text: Otherwise, where would these particulars come from? "Where did my car come from?" True, you cannot say there is an actual car in the *Aibershter*, or in the actual *chesed* a *chesed* to help somebody fix his car. But without it, "you broke the whole *chesed*." To say my car existed inside the *Aibershter* "sounds kind of silly; the *Aibershter* is not made up of cars." To say it did not, "so it's not the *Aibershter*." So where did the car come from? "What, the car came from another *Aibershter*?"

A car? "Yeah, but it's physical." "Yeah, right, and where did this physical come from?" An *Aibershter* and then a physical world beside Him is, the *Rambam* says in *Moreh Nevuchim*, the mistake the Greek philosophers made. Where did the physical world come from? You have to say it was also there.

How, if there is nothing but the *Aibershter*? As all the particulars were in the essential *chesed*. In the *mashal* that is a *chesed* for a particular, not the actual sandwich; in the *nimshal* the actual sandwich came out from there, not a will to give one, separate from Him. Otherwise where would these particulars in the revealed spreading forth come from?

phrases.he: כמו האור וזיו שכלול בעצם השמש, שיש בו בהעלם כל פרטי אופני זיו המתפשט
phrases.en: When the light was inside the sun, it already had all the particular things.

phrases.he: וכהאי גוונא ודי למבין.

blocks.text: When the light was inside the sun it already had all the particulars: the green and blue and yellow you see in the sunlight outside "must have been already inside the sun." "So that's the end of this little section here," the general explanation; now he explains how it comes in three levels.

sections.title: Three levels drawn from the yechida: Yachid, Echad, Kadmon
sections.summary: *Yachid*: powers so wholly within the *yechida* that they *mamash* do not exist. *Echad*: powers ready to come out, like Avraham sitting at his tent with nobody yet come; here they are a unity of many abilities. *Kadmon*: the exact estimate of one act, complete even when something stops it, like the hand already set for the bottle that someone else grabs.

phrases.he: ונמצא ג' מדריגות זה אחר זה נמשך מעצמיות הנפש ממש,
הנקרא בחינת יחידה
הא' י' כחות עצמיים והיוליים,
כמו חפץ חסד העצמי והיולי וכהאי גוונא
כלולים בה בתכלית,
כהתכללות כח התנועה בעצם החי
וכהתכללות התפשטות החיות בעצם כנזכר לעיל
ולא יתכן בהם לומר לשון התאחדות מדברים נבדלים יחד
phrases.en: You can't even say it's a unification.

phrases.he: אחר שכלולים לגמרי בעצם,
והיה כלא היה במציאות כלל וכלל כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: It's like they *mamash* don't exist, totally; like we explained before.

blocks.text: This is *Yachid*. Wholly included in it means they *mamash* do not exist. Like the power of movement in the living being, the *yechida* is not even in their bounds and limits, not in their category, so **you can't even say it's a unification**: "it's like they *mamash* don't exist, totally."

phrases.he: והב' בחינת התפשטות י' כחות שמוכנים לבא בבחינת גלוי
phrases.en: It's a thing of *hispashtus*, that it's *muchan* to come out in various ways, like *chesed* or whatever of the ten *sefiros*.

phrases.he: כמו חפץ חסד העצמי ההיולי שבא לדבר חסד בדרך פרט
גם קודם שנמשך בפועל ממש, רק כשעתיד ומוכן לצאת לדבר פרט
phrases.en: There's a point where it's *muchan* to come out to a *prat*, but you don't have a *prat* yet.

blocks.text: The second is *Echad*. It is already a thing of *hispashtus* (spreading forth): it is ready to come out in various ways, like *chesed*, or whichever of the ten *sefiros*.

blocks.title: Avraham sitting by the tent
blocks.text: Even before it is drawn into actual deed: like *Avraham Avinu* sitting by the tent, ready for a *chesed* to come out, but nothing comes out "because nobody came yet." It is ready to come out to a particular, but there is no particular yet: that is *Echad*.

phrases.he: שם יתכן ענין האחדות מכמה פרטים שבו
phrases.en: There you can say that it's made of various things,

phrases.he: כמו שכל ומדות שבחפץ חסד זה
הנמשך מהעלמות ההיולי הכללי כו'.

blocks.text: **There you can say that it's made of various things**, like the intellect and *middos* in this desire for kindness, though even there it is not *mamash* a unification. If these powers came out of the essence, where they totally did not exist, there is a point where they began to have an ability to exist: "not an actual existence, by the way," just an ability. That is *Echad*, an ability made of many abilities, unified as the general *hispashtus* of the soul.

phrases.he: והג' כשנמשך ובא לאותו דבר פרט,
רק שעדיין לא בא מצד העדר ומניעה

blocks.text: Not only when it does not come; even when it does. When there is no absence and hindrance and you actually do something, this third level is connected to it; but it is *davka* when it does not come, because of an absence and a hindrance, that you can see it.

blocks.title: The bottle on the farbrengen table
blocks.text:
You are at a *farbrengen* (a Chassidic gathering), there is a bottle of vodka on the table, your glass is empty, and you are getting ready to reach for it. The whole movement is already there in the power of movement before you make it; that is why "you don't have to grope around": he knows exactly where his hand will go. Just before he moves, somebody else grabs the bottle.

Two things follow. Nothing happened: it stayed a *hiyuli*, never came out, and yet was completely prepared. ("It's like he was about to do it." "Yeah, it was all prepared in there.") And had he grabbed it, the same preparation connects to the actual grabbing. So the absence he speaks of is not necessarily an absence: that is just how you see it, from the absence and the hindrance.

phrases.he: אבל ההכנה בעצמה כבר בשלימותה,
phrases.en: but the preparation is all complete,

phrases.he: ולא חסר רק לבא בהתגלות בפועל ממש
דהיינו שכבר שיער היטב בעצמו בדרך פרט
לאותו דבר שבא לפועל ממש
והיינו שיער בעצמו בכח מה שצריך להביא בפועל

blocks.text: The preparation itself is already complete, lacking only revelation in actual deed: he has already estimated in himself, in particular, what comes into actual deed, "like to grab the bottle."

sections.title: The examples, and the contraction that brings the spiritual into the physical
sections.summary: The power of movement, the spirit of life and the power of growth each have the three levels, and all three are joined even to the deed: one grabs the bottle with the *yechida* itself. Yet the deed is physical, a different thing, and getting there needs a *tzimtzum*; without it a man freezes, or cannot get a word out.

phrases.he: כמו על דרך דוגמא הנזכר לעיל בכח התנועה
כשעתידה לצאת בגלוי בדבר פרט

blocks.text: The power of movement as it is about to come out, "like to grab a bottle, for instance." So even if he did make the movement, it is connected to this third level.

blocks.title: "When you're finished, pass the bottle over"
blocks.text: The other guy grabbed the bottle, and the power of movement never came into action. So he says, "When you're finished, pass the bottle over." The power of movement, in the essence of the soul just a desire to grab the bottle, really to get himself a drink of vodka, turned into the power of speech, *mamash* the same thing. In *Kadmon* it is *mamash* one, yet one can already speak of powers unified like one. The motivation that had him ready to grab the bottle became telling the guy to pass it.
Both things follow. When it does not happen, you see it was all prepared, yet it need not happen; even when it does happen, the *hiyuli* is still just a *hiyuli*. And one power can turn into another.

phrases.he: וכן מה ששיער התגלות התפשטות רוח החיים,
phrases.en: when he is *meshaer* how much revelation of the *ruach hachayim* is going to be,

phrases.he: והוכן בו מה שעתיד להחיות בפועל ממש
phrases.en: and it's already included what he is *asid lehachayos* in *poel mamash*

blocks.title: "Liven up, we got a big job ahead of us"
blocks.text: When he estimates how much of the spirit of life will be revealed, what he will enliven in actual deed is already included in it: when he psychs himself up to run, say, he needs an extra influx of the spirit of life. For a real heavy action you have to get some extra life, "like they tell the soldiers, liven up, we got a big job ahead of us."

phrases.he: וכמו כן דמיון כח הצומח כשמוכן להצמיח בפועל ממש,
phrases.en: The same thing, like the *koach hatzomeach* in the ground, when it's *mamash* already connected to a tree and it's ready to actually give this tree the power to grow:

phrases.he: שיש בזה גם כן ענין ג' מדריגות הללו
phrases.en: each one of these *kochos* has these three *madreigos*.

blocks.text: So too the power of growth in the ground, *mamash* connected to a tree and ready to give it the power to grow: each power has these three levels, all connected even to the actual deed. The deed is connected not just to *Kadmon*: *Kadmon* is connected to *Echad*, and *Echad* to *Yachid*.

When he grabs for the bottle, "really he's grabbing it with *Yachid*," the essence of the *yechida*, through two conduits: *Echad*, where the powers come out in particular and it is no longer just the essence of the *yechida*; and *Kadmon*, where they come out for this particular action, where the action is estimated.

phrases.he: והכל הוא טרם שבא הדבר עדיין בפועל ממש
כמו התנועה קודם שבאה בגשם הנפעל
או החיות הרוחני קודם שבא בגשם הגוף
ששם משתנה ממהות רוחנית למהות גשם,
phrases.en: Where it actually comes into an actual *tnua*, a *tnua* is not anymore the thing of the soul; it's a physical movement.

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת תנועה גשמיות
phrases.en: That's a physical *tnua*.

phrases.he: והחיות גשמיות
וכהאי גוונא בגשם הצמיחה כו'
phrases.en: the actual plant.

blocks.text: This is not the coming out into actual deed; even when it comes out into the deed, this is the inner power, which does not come into the deed.

Once it comes into an actual movement, the movement is no longer the soul's: it is a physical movement, and the life is physical too. So with the actual plant: "It's not the power of growth at all. It's a different thing, it's a plant. It's like a piece of wood."

phrases.he: שצריך לזה בחינת צמצום וכיווץ בגלוי זה הרוחני בתחלה, כדי שיבוא מכלל רוחניות לגשמיות
phrases.en: In order to come from the spiritual to the physical, you have to make a *tzimtzum*.

phrases.he: (כמו שיתבאר באות הי''ב):
phrases.en: This will be explained, *b'ezras Hashem*, in chapter 12.

blocks.title: Costello and the Wolf Man
blocks.text: A *tzimtzum* and contraction in the spiritual is needed first, for it to come from spirituality into physicality. The example: "Did you ever see Abbott and Costello and the Wolf Man?" (Abbott is the tall one, the straight man.) Costello and Abbott are standing there, the Wolf Man behind Abbott, and Costello goes [he acts out the sputtering]. Why? He is so panicked by the Wolf Man that he cannot *metzamtzem* (contract) his speech into the particular letters; he wants to say the whole speech inside him "at one shot." Since he cannot make a *tzimtzum*, he cannot make the particular thing.

blocks.title: Frozen before a Tyrannosaurus Rex
blocks.text: So too if a Tyrannosaurus Rex looms up over you on the street: people freeze. "You should be running." The shock is so big that the whole power of movement comes out at one shot; he cannot make a *tzimtzum* into a particular movement, which way to go. He tries to run all different ways at once, and so he cannot run any way at all.

So in many, many things. Why, without the *tzimtzum*? The spiritual power is infinite, not for a particular movement, and the power of speech is not for a particular thing; the *tzimtzum* has to go all the way down to the letters.
That is also why people stutter: they are trying to put the whole thought into speech at one shot, without the *tzimtzum*, and you have to teach them to slow down and make a *tzimtzum*.
So to come from the spiritual to the physical you have to make a *tzimtzum*, as will be explained with G-d's help in chapter 12.

Summing up: some places say the *Or Ein Sof* has nothing, "not in the count of ten *sefiros*," "not of any of these attributes at all." Others say "He engraved an engraving in the *tehiru ila'a*," which means letters, "the simple will," "at the head of the King's authority," and "wise, but not with a known wisdom": there is a *chachma*. "So, what's the story?"

No *sefiros* there means not that they are lacking but that it is totally higher than *sefiros*: no more an actual *chachma* there than a will for shoes in a *chesed*. Yet you cannot take them out. Say there is no *chachma*, and "you're actually insulting the *Aibershter*": "He has no *chachma* at all, so the *Aibershter* is stupid." Separate any one *sefira* out and you are a *kofer b'ikar* (one who denies the essence), "*mamash kofer* on the *Aibershter*."

blocks.title: "I don't do shoes"
blocks.text: It is like the *chesed* we spoke of. The guy helps with certain things, but "I don't do shoes." If this poor guy is walking around with bleeding feet and you won't do shoes, "you don't have *chesed*, period." "But I have a fund for coats, and a fund for feeding people. I just won't do shoes." He is standing in front of you with his feet bleeding: you *mamash* don't have *chesed*, you are not an *ish chesed* (a man of kindness), "I don't care what else you do." What, is a *chesed* made up of a *chesed* for shoes? No; but take out this one piece of it and you took out the whole thing.

So too, though there are no ten *sefiros* up there, take out one *sefira*, or a *sefira* of a *sefira*: "I believe there's all these things up there except for *netzach* of *tiferes*," and "you're totally *kofer* in the *ikar*." The basic point of the whole matter: "if not, where would these particulars come from?" "And that's what we learned till now."

reviewQuestions.question: Why does the introduction insist that *hisbonenus* is *iyun* and not meditation, and why must it be done in particulars?
Why is even the name *Yachid* not quite right for the first level?
What does "wise, but not with a known wisdom" mean, and why may one not simply say there is no *chachma* there?
How do the *schnorrers* know a man will help them, and how do they know he will give pants he never gave anyone?
Why is a foundation that gives only shoes no longer a *chesed*, and what does that teach about taking one *sefira* out of the Essence?
What does the bottle of vodka at a *farbrengen* show about *Kadmon*, and what happens when someone else grabs it first?

Sensitivity rule for irreverent wording about G-d: a joke or a phrasing that makes Him sound stupid or unkosher is flagged (the Dumb and Dumber aside, the treif-sandwich line, and "He is stupid, not with a known stupidity"). "So the Aibershter is stupid?" in the end-of-chapter recap is not flagged: there he calls that conclusion an insult.
